name: HTTP authentication (Basic, Digest, Negotiate)
plain: A server can make the browser ask for a username and password.
meaning: Browser shows a native login box and then sends credentials on every request to that realm.

web.api: WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm=...; Authorization header; Negotiate/NTLM for Windows SSO

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: A server can make the browser ask for a username and password.

limits.headline: Can make your browser ask for a username and password in a plain box
limits.user_action: You open a page that is protected, and a login box appears
can: Show a login box from the browser itself
Receive the username and password you type
Send those details again with every request to that part of the site
cannot: Get your saved passwords unless you pick them from the browser box
Hide the box behind a custom design; it is always the browser's own box
Keep you signed in after you close the browser on most setups

story.what_it_is: The server makes your browser pop up a plain username and password box.

marketing.name: HTTP authentication
marketing.pitch: Explains the built in login box that servers can trigger with a challenge, used for simple password protection.

story.for_you: A grey box from the browser itself appears with 'username' and 'password'. After you type, the browser silently resends them on every click on that site until you close it. Many people meet this on staging sites, routers and old company tools.
story.for_makers: It is the quickest way to password protect something with no login page to build. Makers use it for private previews, internal dashboards, device admin pages and simple APIs.

use_cases.example: A web agency hides a client's unfinished site behind a browser login box so only the client can look at it.
A home router or camera admin page asks for a username and password in a plain box when you type its local address.
A company's internal wiki on an old server uses single sign on through the browser, so staff on the work network are let in without typing.
A game studio shares a private playtest build on a password box so only invited testers see the unreleased game.
A reporting tool lets a script fetch data using the same method, so a person and a program use one login style.
A scanner tries common default passwords on these boxes, so the same simple gate that protects can also be attacked.

technical_bounds: Basic sends the password every request
Negotiate uses Kerberos or NTLM only on allowlisted intranet hosts

history.change: Basic and Digest from the start
Credentials in URLs (user:pass@host) blocked for subresources
